name: Flight cap, general officer (solid silver braid)
size_basis: Measured from CAPR 39-1 Fig A5-9 "FLIGHT CAPS" (3 March 2020, p.140) at 157 px/in from the figure's own 1 1/2 in marks. Cap body 12.00 x 4.79 in plus 0.12 in margin. The regulation gives no cap dimensions; real caps vary by size. (Earlier build used the flatter p.139 side silhouette, 11.6 x 3.65 in.)
landmarks_note: rects are {x,y,w,h} in user units (0.01 in); device_slot is a nominal 1 in box centred on the device position (the device itself is 1.15-1.36 in, see the cap-device-* assets)
orientation: side view, front of cap at left (wearer facing left), wearer's left flap shown; sloped crown: tall at the front, lower at the rear (Fig A5-9)
documented: flight cap device on the front left flap, centred halfway between top and bottom of the flap, 1 1/2 in from the front of the cap (6.2.2.2.1-3)
general officers silver braid; other officers silver and blue braid; NCOs and cadets plain blue (6.2.2.2.4-6)
worn slightly to the wearer's right, about one inch above the eyebrows (6.2.2.1)
assumed: braid band width and position (about 0.33 of cap height below the top edge, read off the figure)
navy colour sampled from the figure
figure caps differ slightly in height, each variant keeps its own measured outline

fit.method: per-column profile of the regulation figure

provenance: outline per column from Fig A5-9 (sloped crown, fold line, curtain); braid line traced from the figure; navy and braid colours sampled
name_note: legacy id: women's flight cap (Fig A5-9, p.140); use hat-flight-cap-women-* / hat-flight-cap-men-*
hat_attach_note: garment_attach_center is at the cap outline's own bottom at the centre line (4.43 in from the top of the asset) minus 0.33 in, and the engine puts it on the garment's top_center: at the centre line the cap's lower edge lands 0.33 in below the garment top, over the collar line. The outline bottom is lower toward the front and rear of the cap (0.48 in lower at the lowest point), so the cap overlaps more there. The overlap is estimated (see attach_overlap)

attach_overlap.assumption: The regulation and Fig A5-9 give no relation between the flight cap and the collar (a side view of a cap, no coat). The engine puts garment_attach_center on the garment bounding-box top_center, and the drawn collar does not start there: rendering garment-blues-class-a-coat-female with this cap, the collar top at the centre line (and 0.5 in either side) is 0.27 to 0.30 in below top_center. OVL = 0.30 in measured collar offset + 0.03 in so the lower edge of the cap lands on the collar with no white gap. The cap outline bottom at the centre line is measured from the figure; only the overlap (the cap-to-collar seating, which the regulation does not give) is estimated. The Class B blouse and the FDU carry no collar art at the centre line, their collar points start about 0.1 in lower than the lower edge of the cap there.
